Regarding Lily's symptoms, the combination of migratory joint pain (pain that moves from one joint to another) without visible signs of inflammation like swelling or redness, along with extreme fatigue and low-grade fever, is highly suggestive of **Rheumatic Fever**.

Rheumatic fever is an inflammatory disease that can develop as a complication of inadequately treated strep throat or scarlet fever. The migratory nature of the arthritis (polyarthritis) is a classic hallmark of the condition. Other potential considerations could include viral infections (such as Parvovirus B19 or Hepatitis) or early-stage autoimmune conditions like Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE), but the specific description of migratory pain without swelling strongly points toward Rheumatic Fever.
